findings.chapter: Ch. 4 (The Anatomy of an AI Workload), sidebar table
findings.evidence: Sidebar row label reads "Cloud, 6 hosts — default paid-occupancy input" for the $87,600 / ≈$14.04 per-1K-request line, but the reconciliation on p.91 states the opposite default: "The default rented-fleet unit-cost figure to quote (average traffic, hour-matched basis): (c) ~$0.0033 per request (≈$3.33 per 1K)". The same table cell then says "quote ≈$3.33/1K instead".
findings.issue: Two competing "defaults" for the same 6-host fleet are printed in the same chapter: the table labels the 730-hour paid-occupancy line "default", while the reconciliation paragraph designates the hour-matched $3.33/1K line as the default unit cost. A reader skimming the sidebar can quote $14.04/1K as the default, which the chapter elsewhere calls an "hour-basis artifact".
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the sidebar row to "Cloud, 6 hosts — 730-hour paid-occupancy input (hour-basis artifact)" and reserve the word "default" for the $3.33/1K hour-matched row, so the table and the §4.3 reconciliation use one designation.

findings.evidence: The sidebar table states: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K capex [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 + $1,110.33 energy [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16)". The displayed bracket expression does not arithmetically sum to the displayed total: 21 × ($5,833.3333 + $1,110.33) + $10,000 = 21 × $6,943.6633 + $10,000 = $145,816.93 + $10,000 = $155,816.93 only if you use un-rounded per-host values. But 21 × ($5,833.33 + $1,110.33) + $10,000 = 21 × $6,943.66 + $10,000 = $145,816.86 + $10,000 = $155,816.86 ≠ $155,816.93. The 7-cent discrepancy means the displayed per-host figures, when summed as shown, do not produce the printed total.
findings.issue: The bracket expression uses rounded per-host values ($5,833.33 + $1,110.33 = $6,943.66) that yield $155,816.86 when multiplied by 21 and summed with $10,000, not the stated $155,816.93. The total is only correct if computed from un-rounded intermediates, but the displayed formula as written is off by $0.07.
findings.fix_instruction: Either round the total to match the displayed intermediate values ($155,816.86), or show more precision in the per-host figures (e.g. $1,110.3259), or add a parenthetical note that the total is computed from un-rounded intermediates.

findings.evidence: Page 86, latency bullet: "budget of 1.2 s, comprising retrieval (~120 ms for vector search and reranking on a local GPU) + prefill (budget cap 1.08 s for 9,200 tokens across the 8×H100 canonical host — a budget, not a modeled runtime." The sentence uses an opening parenthesis for the prefill term but the parenthetical is never closed on that line — it continues across multiple sentences including "The cap implies ≈8,500 tokens/s..." and "The minimum GPU count..." before the bullet ends with ") Per Ch 2 and Ch 8)." — a double closing parenthesis with no matching double opening. The sentence structure makes the prefill parenthetical span ~15 sentences, which is difficult to track.
findings.issue: The prefill parenthetical opens with a single '(' but closes with '))' at the end of the bullet, and spans an extremely long run of text (multiple sentences about GPU counts, MFU, and capacity screens). This makes the parenthetical structure unbalanced and hard to follow.
findings.fix_instruction: Break the long parenthetical into a separate sentence or a footnote; ensure parentheses are balanced (one open matches one close).

findings.evidence: The §4.8 mini-case states: "the normative host-count form of Ch 17 Table 17-1 gives ⌈26 ÷ 0.70⌉ = ⌈37.14⌉ = 38 hosts (the occupancy cross-check ⌈430/(17 × 0.7)⌉ = ⌈430/11.9⌉ = ⌈36.13⌉ = 37 sits one host below it) — then 39 hosts before the spare, 40 under the book's provisioning policy, which multiplies the independent ρ = 0.95 as well and adds the N−1 reserve (⌈430/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95)⌉ = ⌈430/11.305⌉ = ⌈38.04⌉ = 39; Ch 17 Table 17-1 adds +1 for the N−1 spare → 40). The same total by the host-count form: with N full-utilization hosts, total (provisioned) = ⌈N ÷ (u × ρ)⌉ = ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ and working = total − 1 — here N = ⌈430/17⌉ = 26, so ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = ⌈39.10⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working." Two different derivations are given for the same 40/39 answer, and the second (the normative one) is presented as 'the same total by the host-count form'. Recomputing: 430/17 = 25.294 → N = 26; 26 ÷ 0.665 = 39.098 → ⌈39.098⌉ = 40; working = 40 − 1 = 39. ✓ The first path: 430/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95) = 430/11.305 = 38.036 → ⌈38.036⌉ = 39, then +1 = 40. ✓ Both reach 40/39, but the passage also states that the occupancy cross-check 'is a bound, not a reproduction of the provisioned total' — which is true at the 37-vs-38 stage, but the 39-vs-40 stage does reproduce it exactly, and the text presents the two as 'two forms' of the same rule while one is declared a cross-check. The prose requires the reader to track four different ceilings (37, 38, 39, 40) with different labels.
findings.issue: The mini-case derives the same 40-host/39-working fleet answer twice through two different arithmetic paths (⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 40 and ⌈430/11.305⌉ = 39 +1 = 40) while simultaneously declaring one of those paths a non-normative 'cross-check' that 'sits one host below' the normative result — a claim true only at the u-only stage, not at the policy stage where the two agree exactly.
findings.fix_instruction: In §4.8, either present only the normative host-count form (⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working) and state the occupancy form once as a bound, or make explicit that at the policy stage the two forms coincide at 40, so the reader is not left with an unqualified 'one host below' statement that the same paragraph's arithmetic contradicts.
